comments: Same as kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_cfar_damp_kernel3_finetune_dropout.json (0.3749/0.3529, a near-tie with plain max-pool's 0.3757/0.3635) but the CFAR peak-detection threshold lowered from alpha=5.0 to alpha=4.0. A finer sweep found alpha=5.0 was not actually optimal: contrast plateaus at ~19.6-20.0 from alpha=4.0 onward (matching or exceeding native resolution's own 19.4x) while recall keeps dropping as alpha increases -- alpha=4.0 gets contrast=19.95 at 95.8% target-pixel recall, strictly dominating alpha=5.0's 19.63 contrast at only 90.0% recall. Fewer real targets erased before the network ever sees them should mean less of a recall ceiling than the alpha=5.0 version had. Same architecture/init/hyperparameters as the original (non-stabilized) cfar_damp run otherwise -- the 'stability fix' (extended QAT schedule + grad clipping) was tested separately and made results worse (0.2993 vs 0.3749), so not reused here.
